basis: Approximate synthesis of grower methods, not a statistical average or one combined recipe. Germination means covered establishment after sowing; first root emergence may be earlier. Blackout means additional loose-cover darkness. Soaking is excluded. Light means elapsed days in the lit growth phase, not continuous illumination. Ranges vary together; do not add all extremes. Buttons retain their selected starter calendar.

crops.name: Black Oil sunflower
crops.note: Approximate light-transition cue; check roots and hull release.
crops.germinationReady: Rooted shoots are lifting the contact tray; pale growth is replacing the blanket of black hulls.
crops.blackoutUse: Remove the load and contact tray. Use a loose dark dome for the chosen stretch method; extra blackout is optional.

crops.name: Daikon Minowase radish
crops.note: Earlier light is also used; do not chase height if stems lean.
crops.germinationReady: Most of the tray has emerged and anchored; pale seedlings outnumber dark hulls.
crops.blackoutUse: Remove the contact tray. Add a loose dark dome only for optional stem stretch; earlier light also works.

crops.name: Waltham 29 broccoli
crops.note: Early-light methods uncover around ½–1 in; 2 in is not required.
crops.germinationReady: Pale seedlings cover most of the tray, roots hold in the coir, and shoots push up the contact tray.
crops.blackoutUse: Remove the contact tray. Use a loose dark dome for optional stretch, or move straight to light.

crops.name: Speckled pea
crops.note: Longer stretch methods vary; move before shoots tangle.
crops.germinationReady: Roots are anchored and shoots have emerged across most of the tray, pushing up the contact cover.
crops.blackoutUse: Remove the contact tray and any load. A loose dark dome is optional; move to light before shoots tangle.

crops.name: Mung beans
crops.note: No grower-verified inch threshold found; use rooted, upright emergence. Timing evidence is limited.
crops.germinationReady: Roots are anchored and shoots stand upright across most of the tray. A tiny root tip alone is too early.
crops.blackoutUse: Remove the contact cover and move to light. This starter uses no extra blackout; the height below is only a rough cue.

G01.title: Microgreen Manager / Piedmont — germination table
G01.finding: Broccoli, Daikon, basic pea and sunflower each have a three-day stacked germination period. Published 2025; this is covered emergence, not time to first root.

G02.title: Microgreen Manager / Piedmont — yield table
G02.finding: Published 2024: broccoli 10 days, Daikon 8, basic pea 9 and sunflower 9 to harvest. Different vintage from G01; light durations inferred across these tables are approximate.

G03.title: Microgreen Manager — separate blackout
G03.finding: Defines blackout as an optional post-germination stretch. Says most crops do not need it; harvesting equipment and stem length affect the choice.

G04.title: On The Grow — broccoli
G04.finding: Two to three days with an empty contact tray, then about one day under a loose dark cover. Light cue includes lifting the tray roughly half an inch; tray lift is not an absolute plant-height measurement.

G05.title: Yardibles — broccoli walkthrough
G05.finding: About three days germination, one to two extra dark days, light at one to two inches, then two to three lit days. This is a longer-stem method, not proof that earlier light fails.

G06.title: Bootstrap Farmer — crop chart
G06.finding: Broccoli and radish: stack two to three days, no separate blackout. Peas: stack two to three plus one to three blackout days. Sunflower: stack two to three plus two to three blackout days. Harvest: 7–10, 7–10, 8–12 and 9–12 days respectively.

G07.title: On The Grow — black-oil sunflower
G07.finding: About four weighted dark days, then one loose blackout day, sometimes another for hulls. Reports eight to ten days overall; roughly three to five lit days is subtraction, not a separately reported duration.

G08.title: Wind River Greens — sunflower
G08.finding: Moves sunflower to light around one to two inches after three to four dark days. Seven to twelve days total. Uses blackout to include covered germination; no additional stretch period is specified.

G09.title: On The Grow — radish
G09.finding: Detailed method keeps contact cover until around day four, adds one blackout day, lights around day five and harvests around day eight or nine. Light phase is therefore about three to four days.

G10.title: True Leaf Market — radish grow guide
G10.finding: Two to four covered germination days plus one to two extra blackout days; stretch stems no taller than about two to two-and-a-half inches. Overall harvest eight to ten days. Generic radish guidance, not a Minowase-specific trial.

G11.title: On The Grow — peas on different trays
G11.finding: 1020 method: about three days contact cover plus one loose blackout day. General summary allows three to five germination days and one to two extra blackout days. Harvest eight to fourteen days; includes Speckled among preferred peas.

G12.title: LaNiTex — pea shoots
G12.finding: Two to three dark days, light at two to three centimetres (about 0.8–1.2 inches), ten to sixteen days to a later tendril harvest. Different harvest target from a young Speckled crop.

G13.title: MP Seeds — mung bean microgreens
G13.finding: Microgreen prose: three to four days germination and another three in light. Product table says three to four blackout days and eight to nine total. These are overlapping dark-stage labels, not two sequential dark periods; timing is internally inconsistent.

G14.title: Vitality Farms — Growing Micros, mung p. 40 and radish p. 42
G14.finding: Mung: three to four stacked days then about seven lit days, conflicting with its seven-to-ten-day harvest heading. Radish: two to four stacked days then three to four lit days. Contributed recipes are not independently replicated trials.

G15.title: On The Grow — weight to blackout visual cues
G15.finding: Uses a predominance of pale seedling growth over dark hulls and shoots beginning to bend under the contact cover to remove pressure. Loose blackout is optional; finish while stems support themselves. No universal start-blackout height is specified. Pea and mung card wording uses rooted emergence rather than hull colour.

transitionBasis: No verified universal height for starting loose blackout. Use tray-wide rooted emergence rather than the first root tip or a fixed day. The illustrated cues are an editorial synthesis, not a germination-percentage test; seed colour and tray lift vary by method. End stretch while shoots still support themselves.
